## Preserved inaccurate classification

The first cancelled-reversal inspection is a **complete native semantic
refusal**, not an operational failure. Its client, wrapper and native return
codes are all 1; its native stdout is exactly
`qleisli.hierarchy-pending 3\nerror\ninvalid_ir\n`. All 12,092 stdin bytes were
written, and capture `reason` and `error` are null. The frozen summary and
skipped-request reason `client incomplete/operational failure` came from a
generic successful-result predicate and misclassify this record. Those original
bytes remain unchanged; this additive clarification and raw records determine
the accurate account. This case earns no valid-artifact reversal-contract
negative evidence.

The actual `Layout.PortsMatch` condition preserves the ordered coordinates
inside one complete typed Bits2 owner. Reversing only its positional rewire
fails that condition even though the map is bijective. A separate unexecuted
`reversal-negative-02` proposal retains this failed first attempt and reuses
the existing actual take/put reversal through legal boundary rewires. Its later
inspection and unchanged-request outcomes must be recorded afresh.

## Scope

These observations establish only the particular independently requested
payload/request gate outcomes shown above. They do not prove the producer's
source preservation, arbitrary-size QFT, a public std API, decoder/runtime
correspondence, PR, quantitative RS or a constitutional guarantee. Existing
conditional Fourier mathematics is retained; no fresh Lean build, audit or
replay occurred in this fixture-only unit. All24 #317 criteria stay open;
